backgrounds:acolyte/desc: You served in a temple whose god may have died long ago.
backgrounds:criminal/desc: You know the alleys of ten cities, and you owe debts in every one of them.
backgrounds:sage/desc: Years in the archives taught you that every truth has a footnote.
backgrounds:soldier/desc: You fought in a war whose purpose nobody remembers anymore.
barks:dorn/0/text: Warm beer, cold beds! Or the other way round, if you prefer.
barks:dorn/1/text: Whoever doesn't sleep at the Crooked Hinge sleeps in the gutter.
barks:hask/0/text: No contract, no trade. No trade, no Zawias.
barks:hask/1/text: The gate spat someone out again. Probably you.
barks:hask/2/text: I heard about the alley. The Inscribed saw nothing, understand?
barks:kwit/0/text: Sign here, here and... here. Reality won't record itself.
barks:kwit/1/text: Every rumor has a price. Most of them are cheap.
barks:lis/0/text: Every stone in this market remembers more than we do.
barks:lis/1/text: The letters are fleeing the books again. Something is coming.
barks:mirela/0/text: Keys! Keys for doors you haven't met yet!
barks:mirela/1/text: Three locks. I forged them myself. Three!
barks:mirela/2/text: Zawias remembers who brings keys back.
barks:odzwierny/1/text: Don't stand so close to the door, wanderer.
barks:pchla/1/text: Don't look at me like that, I didn't steal anything. Today.
barks:pchla/2/text: Remember, you didn't hear it from me.
classes:cleric/choice/options/protector/: Proficiency with heavy armor and martial weapons. You start in chain mail.
classes:cleric/choice/options/thaumaturg: An extra cantrip. You add your Wisdom modifier to Arcana and Religion checks.
classes:cleric/desc: A vessel of faith. In a city where belief shapes the world, that is a mighty weapon.
classes:fighter/choice/options/dueling/d: +2 damage with a one-handed weapon and no other weapon.
classes:fighter/choice/options/great_wea: Rolls of 1-2 on damage dice count as 3.
classes:fighter/desc: A master of weapons and armor. Tough, with a rich choice of tactics.
classes:rogue/desc: A shadow with a knife. Sneak Attack, Expertise and elusiveness.
classes:wizard/desc: A scholar of the arcane with a spellbook. Fragile, but changes the course of a fight.
conditions:blinded/desc: You have disadvantage on attacks, and attacks against you have advantage.
conditions:frightened/desc: You have disadvantage on attacks and checks.
conditions:incapacitated/desc: You can't take actions or reactions.
conditions:paralyzed/desc: You are incapacitated and can't move or speak. Attacks against you have advantage, and a melee hit from close by is a critical hit. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saves.
conditions:poisoned/desc: You have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
conditions:prone/desc: You have disadvantage on attacks. Melee attacks against you have advantage, ranged attacks have disadvantage.
conditions:restrained/desc: Speed 0. You have disadvantage on attacks, and attacks against you have advantage.
conditions:unconscious/desc: You are incapacitated and prone. Attacks against you have advantage, and a melee hit from close by is a critical hit.
dialogues/arch:nodes/portal/effects/2/jo: I opened a door that didn't exist. Zawias will never be the same.
dialogues/arch:nodes/portal/text: The key turns in the void and something clicks shut. A door appears beneath the arch that a moment ago did not exist. It is made of your story. It swings open, and a wind blows through smelling of a place no atlas of the planes has ever charted.
dialogues/arch:nodes/runes/text: The runes aren't a record but a question. The arch is waiting for an answer that doesn't exist yet. In the very middle of the keystone there is a small hollow shaped like a keyhole.
dialogues/arch:nodes/runes_fail/text: The runes blur whenever you try to focus on them. It gives you a headache.
dialogues/arch:nodes/start/choices/0/tex: Study the runes on the stone.
dialogues/arch:nodes/start/text: A stone arch, taller than two men, stands in the middle of the market. Beneath it there is nothing but the market seen from the other side. Merchants give it a wide berth, though nobody remembers why.
dialogues/arch:nodes/with_key/choices/0/: Raise the key and turn it in the empty air beneath the arch.
dialogues/arch:nodes/after_portal/text: The market's cobbles are visible beneath the arch again. A warm trace of the crossing remains in the notch in the keystone.
dialogues/arch:nodes/with_key/text: The key in your hand grows hot. Its teeth turn, go still, and point at the keystone. The air beneath the arch trembles like the surface of water.
dialogues/arch:nodes/wanderer_memory/tex: As you bring the key close to the stone, the Arch calls up the first gate of Zawias. It is your hand that cuts three marks into the keystone. It is you they call the Wanderer and ask for leave to cross. You hear your own voice: "I give my name to the gate. The road belongs to those who walk it." The key kept that memory. Now the Arch waits for you to decide whether to open it.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/caught/text: A board creaks underfoot. The mephit shrieks like a nail dragged across tin. The cultist leaps to his feet.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/force_fail/text: The door doesn't even budge. You rub your aching shoulder.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/forced/text: The door flies off its hinges with a crash they probably heard on the far side of the ring. Shouts rise from inside.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/lock_fail/text: The pick bends with a faint snap. This lock is sturdier than it looked. You may have jammed it.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/picked/choices/: Sneak to the chest and take the key.
Back away quietly and leave the door ajar.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/picked/text: The lock gives with a quiet click. You ease the door open. In the warehouse gloom a cultist dozes against a crate, and a small creature of rust and dust circles beneath the ceiling. Sever's chest stands right by the entrance.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/start/text: A rusty, iron-bound door with a heavy lock. From behind it comes a faint scratching, as if claws were scraping metal.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/stolen/effects/: I stole the key from the Unravelers' warehouse through the back door. Nobody saw me.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/stolen/text: You slip between the shadows. The lid of the chest doesn't creak. Under the rags lies a brass key, warm as a living thing. Its teeth turn toward you. You leave as quietly as you came.
dialogues/chest:nodes/caught/text: The lid creaks horribly. Every head in the warehouse turns toward you.
dialogues/chest:nodes/empty/text: Empty. Only threads and rust remain.
dialogues/chest:nodes/loot/choices/1/tex: Take the gold and the potion.
dialogues/chest:nodes/loot/text: In the chest, under a heap of unpicked threads, lie a brass key warm as a living creature, a coin purse and a vial of red liquid.
dialogues/chest:nodes/start/text: An iron-bound chest covered in rusty dust. The Unravelers are right next to it.
dialogues/chest:nodes/stolen/effects/6/j: I stole the key from the chest of Sever the Unraveler.
dialogues/chest:nodes/stolen/text: Your fingers find warm brass under the rags. Nobody looks up.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/rested/text: You sleep like a stone. In Zawias there is no day or night, only the light seeping from beyond the ring. You wake up rested.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/rumors/text: "The Unravelers are prowling around the old warehouse in the east again. Lately they've been paying some thugs to watch the alley. And Mirela's been walking around like she's been poisoned since morning. You didn't hear it from me."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/start/choices/0/tex: I need a bed. (2 gp, long rest)
dialogues/dorn:nodes/start/choices/1/tex: What's the gossip around the market?
dialogues/dorn:nodes/start/text: A broad-shouldered innkeeper wipes a tankard with a rag that has seen better planes. "The Crooked Hinge. A bed, beer, warm food. And gossip, if you're buying."
dialogues/hask:nodes/custodian/choices/0: I see. I have other questions.
dialogues/hask:nodes/custodian/text: Hask lowers his voice. "You don't talk about her out loud. She makes sure doors open only for those they should. Whoever plays with keys they don't understand simply… vanishes. Nobody kills them. A door lets them in and never lets them out."
dialogues/hask:nodes/factions/text: "The Inscribed. We believe reality is a contract, and anything can be negotiated if enough people sign. Belief has weight here, stranger. Here convictions truly change the world. Then there's the Echo, who collect stories, because identity is only a story. And the Unravelers." He grimaces. "They believe everything falls apart, and that it's a good thing."
dialogues/hask:nodes/insight_fail/text: "What's bothering me is that you ask too many questions." Hask shifts his grip on his spear.
dialogues/hask:nodes/insight_ok/text: Hask sighs. "You're sharp. Mirela, the keysmith on the north side of the market, was robbed last night. Something went missing that shouldn't have been in any display case. The Inscribed would rather stay out of it; it's not our contract. But if you're looking for work, go see her."
dialogues/hask:nodes/start/choices/1/tex: Who are the ones with the quill seal? The Inscribed?
dialogues/hask:nodes/start/choices/2/tex: Something's bothering you. I can see it.
dialogues/hask:nodes/start/choices/3/tex: How do I survive my first day here?
dialogues/hask:nodes/start/choices/5/tex: [Hand over Kwit's contract] Clear the Unravelers out of the eastern alley.
dialogues/hask:nodes/start/choices/6/tex: Does the gate always leave a mark like this on your hand?
dialogues/hask:nodes/wanderer_trace/text: Hask turns your hand over. Three pale lines run across your skin, just like the cuts on the inside of the gate. "I've only ever seen that mark on the keystone. It's always been there. Show it to Lis at the Archive of the Echo."
dialogues/hask:nodes/clear_alley/text: Hask checks the seal and tucks the parchment under his breastplate. "One favor. Agreed." He whistles for the patrol. The guards head east and return a short while later. "The thugs scattered. The alley is clear all the way to the warehouse's back door."
dialogues/hask:nodes/clear_alley/effects: I gave Hask Kwit's contract. The patrol drove the thugs out of the eastern alley. I can reach the warehouse's back door safely.
dialogues/hask:nodes/start/text: A guard in scale armor looks you up and down. His breastplate bears an embossed seal: a hand holding a quill. "New? The gate spits out your kind every quarter hour. Welcome to the Rusty Market. Don't touch anything you haven't paid for."
dialogues/hask:nodes/tips/text: "Click where you want to go, and you go. Click on someone to talk to them. In a fight everyone takes turns: move, action, bonus action, reaction, like any decent killing. You can take a short rest anywhere with R. For a proper sleep, see Dorn at the inn. And save your fate with F5, because Zawias doesn't forgive."
dialogues/hask:nodes/where/text: "In Zawias. A ring-city hanging in the crack between the planes. Any door can become a gate if you carry the right key. It can be an object, a word, a memory or a regret. The city is ruled by the Curator. Nobody has seen her, and whoever tried won't see anything ever again."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/bluff_exposed/effec: After the patrol returned the contract, Kwit checked the register and uncovered my lie. The Inscribed distrust me. Kwit now charges more for a potion.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/bluff_exposed/text: Kwit lays the patrol's receipt in front of you. "Hask returned the contract. I checked the register. The Curator sent no one. I've entered your name. From now on, my prices for you include a risk surcharge."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/arch/text: "The Doorless Arch. The oldest thing in the market, older than the market itself. It isn't in our register, because nobody ever signed for it. That is troubling."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/info/choices/1/text: I'll offer another deal: I'll tell you who's asking questions about you.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/info/choices/2/text: The Curator sent me. Don't keep her waiting.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/info/text: "I know. Information is a commodity, and a commodity has a price. Ten gold pieces."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/lead/effects/2/jour: Kwit claims the Unravelers from the warehouse in the east and their leader Sever are behind the theft.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/lead/text: Kwit writes something down, sets his quill aside and for the first time looks you in the eye. "Rusty dust is what the Unravelers leave behind. They hole up in the old warehouse at the eastern edge of the market. Their leader, Sever, talks about 'unraveling promises'. A key is a promise. Work out the rest yourself."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/lead_scared/effects: Kwit pointed me to the Unravelers' warehouse and gave me a contract of the Inscribed. Hask by the gate can take it in exchange for clearing the eastern alley.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/lead_scared/text: The quill slips from his fingers. "I… of course. The Unravelers. The old warehouse in the east. Sever. Please tell the Curator that the Inscribed always cooperate."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/no_deal/text: "No." The quill scratches again. "Ten pieces or goodbye."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/philosophy/text: "Reality is a contract. Gravity works because everyone agreed to it. When enough people sign under some truth, it becomes law. We merely… keep the register."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/philosophy2/text: Kwit smiles thinly. "Then their truth weighs less. And in Zawias, whatever weighs less is easily blown away."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/start/choices/0/tex: Mirela was robbed. What do you know about it?
dialogues/kwit:nodes/start/choices/2/tex: What's that arch in the middle of the market?
dialogues/kwit:nodes/start/choices/4/tex: Do you have a healing potion for sale?
dialogues/kwit:nodes/supplies/text: Kwit takes a vial of red liquid from under his desk and opens the register.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/supplies/choices/0/: [5 gp, trusted rate] I'll buy the healing potion.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/supplies/choices/1/: [10 gp] I'll buy the healing potion.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/supplies/choices/2/: [20 gp, including risk surcharge] I'll buy the healing potion.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/supplies_bought/tex: Kwit records the payment and slides the vial toward you.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/start/text: A thin man in a grey frock coat keeps writing, even while he looks at you. The quill scratches. "Kwit, notary of the Inscribed. Every conversation is a contract, and a contract has a price. How may I serve?"
dialogues/lis:nodes/arcana_fail/text: The letters flee from your gaze and huddle in the corner of the page. Lis closes the book. "Not every story wants to be read."
dialogues/lis:nodes/arcana_ok/effects/3/: The key opens a door that doesn't exist yet. Lis suggested an argument for Sever: an unfulfilled possibility is entropy too.
dialogues/lis:nodes/arcana_ok/text: The letters settle under your gaze. "You see? This key has no door because its door doesn't exist yet. Whoever believes in it first will open it. To the Unravelers that's blasphemy. But if you tell Sever that an unfulfilled possibility is pure entropy, he might listen. Decay that hasn't started yet is still decay."
dialogues/lis:nodes/companion/choices/1/: Go back to the Archive. I'll go on alone.
dialogues/lis:nodes/companion/choices/2/: Do you know this mark from the gate? I have it on my hand.
dialogues/lis:nodes/start/choices/6/text: Do you know this mark from the gate? I have it on my hand.
dialogues/lis:nodes/wanderer_record/text: Lis opens the book of crossings. You find a drawing of three lines and a note: "The Wanderer gave their name to the gate. From this day, no keeper shall hold a road for themselves." There is a blank beneath the entry. "The memory of that day was sealed in the key," Lis says. "If you retrieve it, see whether it answers you."
dialogues/lis:nodes/wanderer_record/choi: I'll find out when I recover the key.
dialogues/lis:nodes/companion/text: Lis walks beside you, scribbling something as she goes. "The story runs on. Where to now?"
dialogues/lis:nodes/echo/text: "Identity is the story you tell about yourself. Change the story and you change yourself. Steal someone's story and you steal them. We collect stories and keep them so nobody loses them… and so nobody steals them."
dialogues/lis:nodes/join/text: Lis closes the book and looks at you for a moment, as if reading a page nobody has written yet. "The Key Without a Door is a story that wants to end. I want to be there when it does. I'll come with you."
dialogues/lis:nodes/key/effects/2/journa: Lis from the Archive of the Echo says the Unravelers want to destroy the key. They hole up in the old warehouse.
dialogues/lis:nodes/key/text: "Ah, the Key Without a Door. A beautiful story, still unfinished. The Unravelers want to cut it short. They believe unfulfilled promises are the worst kind of lie and must be unraveled. Their nest is in the old warehouse in the east."
dialogues/lis:nodes/leave/text: "I'll write down everything I saw. You know where to find me." Lis walks off toward the Archive.
dialogues/lis:nodes/start/choices/1/text: I'm looking for a stolen key. The Key Without a Door.
dialogues/lis:nodes/start/choices/2/text: Let me look at the records about that key.
dialogues/lis:nodes/start/choices/3/text: You want a story? I'll tell you where I came from.
dialogues/lis:nodes/start/choices/4/text: Will you come with me? This story isn't over yet.
dialogues/lis:nodes/start/text: A woman with hair the color of old paper sits on the steps of the Archive with an open book on her knees. The letters on the pages crawl like ants. "Everyone who comes here brings a story. What's yours?"
dialogues/lis:nodes/story/text: You tell her about the world you came from. Lis listens with her eyes closed while the letters in the book dance. "A good story. Here, this is for it." She touches your forehead and you feel a surge of confidence.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/accept/choices/0/: I'll be back with the key.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/accept/effects/2/: Mirela asked me to recover the Key Without a Door. I should ask Kwit, Flea and Lis.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/accept/text: "Take this." She presses a vial of red liquid into your hand. "Ask around the market. Kwit from the Chancery knows everything, but he charges for it. Flea, the little one by the eastern alley, sees everything. And Lis from the Archive of the Echo knows every story about keys."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/done/text: "Back again? Need a key? A discount for you. A small one."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/hints/text: "Kwit at the Chancery of the Inscribed in the west. Flea by the eastern alley. Lis at the Archive of the Echo in the south. Rusty dust… Whoever leaves rust behind wants everything to fall apart."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/keep/effects/2/jo: I kept the Key Without a Door. Mirela says it fits the Arch in the middle of the market.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/keep/text: "You thief! You… No. You know what? Go. May a door let you in and never let you out." She turns her back on you.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/kept/text: Mirela won't even look at you.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/progress/choices/: Who was I supposed to ask?
dialogues/mirela:nodes/progress/text: "Well? Have you got it? No? Then why are you standing here instead of looking?"
dialogues/mirela:nodes/return/choices/1/: Here's your key. A hundred and fifty, as agreed.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/return/choices/2/: First tell me what it really opens.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/return/choices/3/: I'll keep it a while longer.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/return/text: Mirela freezes when she sees the key in your hand. Its teeth move slowly, as if searching for something. "You have it… Give it back. Please."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/returned/effects/: I gave the key back to Mirela. Something tells me this story isn't over.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/wanderer_memory/t: The key burns in your hand. For a moment you see the first gate of Zawias. It is your hand that cuts three lines into the keystone. It is you they call the Wanderer and ask for leave to cross. You hear yourself take an oath: "I give my name to the gate. The road belongs to those who walk it." The memory fades. Mirela notices the key has stopped shaking. "You can give it back. Or you can find out who the Arch is waiting for now."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/returned/text: Mirela clutches the key to her chest as if holding a child. "Thank you. Zawias will remember this favor. I certainly will."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/reward/choices/1/: I'm risking my skin for a key that's 'alive'. A hundred and fifty.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/reward/text: "A hundred gold pieces. Fair, by market standards."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/reward_no/text: "A hundred. Or I'll find someone cheaper, and there's one on every corner."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/reward_plus/text: Mirela purses her lips and counts something on her fingers. "A hundred and fifty. But not a copper more."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/start/text: A woman with fingers blackened by brass shifts keys from one pile to another, as if she needed something to do. There must be a hundred of them hanging around her neck. "Not buying? Then don't waste my… Wait. You've got the face of someone who isn't afraid of alleys."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/theft/choices/0/t: The Key Without a Door? What's that?
dialogues/mirela:nodes/theft/choices/1/t: I'll help you get it back.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/theft/choices/2/t: And what's in it for me?
dialogues/mirela:nodes/theft/text: "Someone stole the Key Without a Door. From my display case, from under three locks I forged myself! All they left was rusty dust on the velvet."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/truth/choices/2/t: I'll keep it. I'll see for myself what's behind that door.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/truth/text: Mirela lowers her eyes. "The arch in the middle of the market. The one without a door. It's always stood there and opens nothing, because its door doesn't exist yet. This key can… create it. I was going to sell it to the highest bidder. The Curator would never forgive me, but gold is gold."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/truth_fail/choice: I'll keep it a while longer.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/truth_fail/text: "It opens what it's meant to open. I'm a keysmith, not a philosopher." She holds out her hand.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/what_key/choices/: And what's in it for me?
dialogues/mirela:nodes/what_key/text: "In Zawias every key is a promise: somewhere there's a door it will open. This one is a promise with no address. It doesn't fit any lock I know, and I know them all. But it's alive. It's warm. It's searching."
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/threat/text: The Doorkeeper doesn't reach for a weapon. He whistles through his teeth, two short notes. Behind the door the talking stops, and then come footsteps, a lot of footsteps. "Unravel me, you say? Come on, then. Let's see who falls apart first."
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/threat/choices: I threatened the Doorkeeper and backed off when the warehouse filled with Unravelers behind the door. Now he knows my face. That leaves the back door from the east alley, or forcing my way in once I'm stronger.
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/fight_node/tex: The Doorkeeper grins wide, baring blackened teeth, and draws a sickle. "Finally, something interesting." Shuffling comes from behind the door.
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/let_in/text: The Doorkeeper studies you for a long time, then steps away from the door. "Go in. Sever likes people who fall apart out of curiosity."
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/refuse/text: "Sever doesn't talk to strangers. Leave while you're still in one piece."
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/start/choices/: I've come to talk to Sever. About the key.
I have a message for Sever from someone higher up.
Show the Rust Token. "The brothers from the alley send their regards."
Get out of my way or I'll unravel you myself.
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/start/text: A man in a robe with threads deliberately unpicked leans against the warehouse door. A rusty tin plate hangs around his neck. "Everything falls apart, stranger. Your plans too. What do you want?"
dialogues/pchla:nodes/alley/text: "A shortcut to the old warehouse. Round the back. The back door's got a lock any old pick will open, if you've got nimble fingers."
dialogues/pchla:nodes/paid/effects/5/jou: Flea warned me about an ambush in the alley. The Unravelers hole up in the warehouse beyond it.
dialogues/pchla:nodes/paid/text: Flea glances around quickly. "It's the Unravelers. The warehouse at the end, past the alley. But listen, this part's free: two thugs with a crossbow are waiting in the alley. They get paid to grab anyone who asks about the key. Go in with a weapon in your hand, not your mouth."
dialogues/pchla:nodes/scared/effects/5/j: Flea warned me about an ambush in the alley. The Unravelers hole up in the warehouse beyond it.
dialogues/pchla:nodes/scared/text: Flea goes pale. "Fine, fine. The Unravelers gave me a copper to tell them who's sniffing around. But you're all right. Two of them are waiting in the alley. The warehouse is further on, past them. Don't say it was me."
dialogues/pchla:nodes/snitch/text: "I don't know nothing, I didn't see nothing." Flea shrugs, and when you turn away you hear quick footsteps behind you heading for the alley.
dialogues/pchla:nodes/start/choices/0/te: Know anything about the theft at Mirela's? (5 gp)
dialogues/pchla:nodes/start/choices/1/te: Something's bothering you. You look scared.
dialogues/pchla:nodes/start/choices/2/te: Spill what you know, or you'll regret it.
dialogues/pchla:nodes/start/text: A boy in a coat far too big for him flips a copper without looking at it. "What? I'm not small, I'm cheap."
dialogues/sever:nodes/after/text: "Go now. Don't disturb me while I fall apart."
dialogues/sever:nodes/angry/text: Sever stands. "Words fall apart too." He raises his hand, and the air behind him cracks like glass. "Unravel them."
dialogues/sever:nodes/convinced/effects/: I convinced Sever, and he gave me the key without a fight.
dialogues/sever:nodes/convinced/text: Sever falls silent. The dust stops trickling from his fingers. Then he laughs dryly, as if something inside him cracked. "A possibility that rots before it's born… You're right. Let it fall apart on its own." He tosses you the key. "Take it. Watch it die."
dialogues/sever:nodes/scared/effects/5/j: I intimidated Sever and he gave me the key.
dialogues/sever:nodes/scared/text: The cracks on Sever's face darken. "Fear is decay too. Interesting." He tosses you the key. "Take it. It will return to dust anyway."
dialogues/sever:nodes/start/choices/0/te: Why do you want to destroy it?
dialogues/sever:nodes/start/choices/1/te: The Key Without a Door is a possibility that may never come true. That's pure entropy, decay already underway. Destroying it unravels nothing, it only ends it.
dialogues/sever:nodes/start/choices/2/te: Even gods die, Sever. Let the key fall apart on its own, in someone's hands. That would be truer.
dialogues/sever:nodes/start/choices/3/te: Hand over the key, or I'll personally unravel every cracked piece of you.
dialogues/sever:nodes/start/text: A tall man sits on a chest, his face covered in a web of fine cracks like old porcelain. Rusty dust trickles between his fingers. "You've come for the key. Do you know what it is? A promise. And a promise is a lie that hasn't rotted yet."
dialogues/sever:nodes/why/choices/0/text: I understand your point of view.
dialogues/sever:nodes/why/text: "Everything falls apart: stars, planes, gods. That's not a tragedy, it's the honesty of the universe. But this key pretends it can begin something. Open a door that isn't there. That's a lie, and the worst kind, because it gives hope. We will unravel it."
encounters:ambush/intro: Two figures step out of the alley's shadow. "Someone's far too interested in other people's keys."
encounters:ambush/on_victory/3/journal: The alley thugs carried a Rust Token. It's the sign of the Unravelers, who hole up in the old warehouse.
encounters:warehouse/intro: Sever raises a hand. "Everything falls apart. So will you."
encounters:warehouse/on_victory/3/journa: The Unravelers in the warehouse are beaten, and Sever escaped through a crack in reality. The key should be in his chest.
features:action_surge/desc: Once per short rest you gain an extra action on your turn.
features:alert/desc: You add your proficiency bonus to Initiative.
features:arcane_recovery/desc: During a short rest you recover spell slots with a combined level of up to half your level.
features:channel_divinity/desc: Two uses; a short rest restores one.
features:cunning_action/desc: Bonus action: Dash, Disengage or Hide.
features:disciple_of_life/desc: Healing spells restore an extra 2 + spell level HP.
features:divine_spark/desc: Action: heal 1d8 + WIS HP, or deal that much radiant damage (half on a successful CON save).
features:dwarven_resilience/desc: Resistance to poison damage; advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.
features:evocation_savant/desc: Extra evocation spells in your spellbook.
features:expertise/desc: Double proficiency bonus in two skills.
features:fast_hands/desc: You can use an object or thieves' tools as a bonus action.
features:fey_ancestry/desc: Advantage on saving throws against being charmed.
features:fiendish_legacy/desc: Resistance to fire; you know Fire Bolt.
features:fighting_style/desc: A combat specialty chosen at character creation.
features:improved_critical/desc: You score a critical hit on a roll of 19-20.
features:life_domain_spells/desc: Bless and Cure Wounds are always prepared.
features:magic_initiate_cleric/desc: You know the Sacred Flame cantrip.
features:magic_initiate_wizard/desc: You know the Fire Bolt cantrip.
features:potent_cantrip/desc: Your damaging cantrips deal half damage even on a miss or a successful save.
features:remarkable_athlete/desc: You have advantage on Initiative and Athletics checks.
features:resourceful/desc: You gain Heroic Inspiration after a long rest.
features:ritual_adept/desc: You cast ritual spells from your book without preparing them.
features:savage_attacker/desc: Once per turn you roll a weapon's damage dice twice and use the better result.
features:second_wind/desc: Bonus action: regain 1d10 + level HP. Two uses; a short rest restores one.
features:sneak_attack/desc: Once per turn you deal extra d6 damage when you have advantage or an ally stands next to the target. Requires a finesse or ranged weapon.
features:spellcasting/desc: You cast spells using spell slots.
features:steady_aim/desc: Bonus action if you haven't moved: advantage on your next attack, but your speed drops to 0.
features:tactical_mind/desc: When you fail an ability check, you can spend a Second Wind to add 1d10.
features:thieves_cant/desc: The secret language of thieves and smugglers.
features:trance/desc: You don't sleep; magic can't put you to sleep.
features:weapon_mastery/desc: You can use the mastery properties of your weapons (Sap, Vex, Topple, Graze...).
items:key_without_door/desc: A brass key, warm to the touch. Its teeth keep changing shape, as if searching for a lock.
items:kwit_contract/desc: Parchment bearing Kwit's seal. Give it to Hask by the gate to have the patrol clear the eastern alley.
items:potion_healing/desc: Restores 2d4+2 HP. Drinking it is a bonus action.
items:rust_token/desc: A rusty tin plate stamped with an unraveled knot. The recognition sign of the Unravelers.
items:thieves_tools/desc: Picks and files. They let you open locks.
maps/rusty_market:name: Rusty Market
monsters:rust_mephit/attacks/1/desc: A cloud of rusty dust. A target that fails a Dexterity saving throw (DC 10) is blinded.
species:dwarf/desc: They forge iron that doesn't rust even here, and make a good living from it.
species:elf/desc: They remember planes that no longer exist. They don't sleep; they meditate in a trance.
species:human/desc: Humans are the most numerous folk in Zawias. Each came here from another world, and nobody knows why.
species:tiefling/desc: The legacy of the Lower Planes runs in their blood. In Zawias they draw less suspicion than anywhere else.
spells:bless/desc: Up to three allies add 1d4 to attack rolls and saving throws. Requires concentration.
spells:burning_hands/desc: A 4.5 m cone of fire deals 3d6 fire damage. A successful Dexterity save halves it.
spells:chromatic_orb/desc: A sphere of shimmering energy. Spell attack: 3d8 acid damage.
spells:cure_wounds/desc: A creature you touch regains 2d8 + your spellcasting modifier HP.
spells:fire_bolt/desc: Ranged spell attack. Deals 1d10 fire damage.
spells:guiding_bolt/desc: Ranged spell attack for 4d6 radiant damage. The next attack against the target has advantage.
spells:healing_word/desc: Bonus action. A creature in range regains 2d4 + your spellcasting modifier HP.
spells:hold_person/desc: A humanoid must make a Wisdom saving throw or be paralyzed. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. Concentration.
spells:inflict_wounds/desc: The target makes a Constitution saving throw: 2d10 necrotic damage on a failure, half on a success.
spells:light/desc: An object sheds light like a torch.
spells:magic_missile/desc: Three darts, each dealing 1d4+1 force damage. They never miss.
spells:prestidigitation/desc: Minor magical tricks. Useful for impressing whoever you're talking to.
spells:ray_of_frost/desc: Ranged spell attack. Deals 1d8 cold damage, and the target's speed drops by 3 m until the start of your next turn.
spells:sacred_flame/desc: The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure it takes 1d8 radiant damage.
spells:shatter/desc: A deafening crash at a chosen point (3 m radius). Constitution save: 3d8 thunder damage, half on a success.
spells:shield/desc: Reaction to being hit. You gain +5 AC until the start of your next turn, which can turn a hit into a miss.
spells:sleep/desc: Creatures within 1.5 m of a chosen point make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure they fall into a magical sleep that damage breaks.
spells:thaumaturgy/desc: Minor wonders: a voice like thunder, flickering flames. Handy in conversations.
spells:thunderwave/desc: A wave of thunderous force in front of you. Constitution save: 2d8 thunder damage, half on a success.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/lock_fail/effec: I jammed the lock on the warehouse back door. I can still force it, or try the front door past the Doorkeeper.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/force_fail/effe: I couldn't force the warehouse back door. The Doorkeeper guards the front. I can persuade him, trick him or go in by force.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/no_deal/effects/0/j: Kwit won't say anything for free; he wants ten coins. Flea or Lis at the Archive of the Echo may know the same about the theft.
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/refuse/effects: The Doorkeeper wouldn't let me into the warehouse. There's also a back door on the east alley side. Or I could go in by force.
dialogues/pchla:nodes/snitch/effects/2/j: Flea told me nothing and ran off toward the east alley. I can still ask Kwit or Lis at the Archive of the Echo about the theft.
barks:hask/3/text: Kwit says you pay on time. That's rare in this market.
barks:hask/4/text: The patrol has its eye on you, newcomer. No tricks.
barks:kwit/2/text: For regular clients the ink drips less.
barks:kwit/3/text: Your name is in the register. In red.
barks:lis/2/text: Your story is already making the rounds in the Archive. People ask about you.
barks:lis/3/text: Every stone in this market has a story. Most of them are boring.
barks:lis/4/text: I can smell rust in the air. The Unravelers are close.
barks:lis/5/text: This Arch asks a question. I'd like to hear how you answer it.
barks:lis/6/text: Flea warned us. Let's not get caught off guard in the alley.
barks:lis/7/text: Kwit's contract? The Curator doesn't like people signing in her name.
barks:lis/8/text: That token opens some doors and closes others. Be careful who you show it to.
barks:lis/9/text: The Wanderer… the Echo wrote you down long ago. Now I understand why the mark called to you.
barks:odzwierny/2/text: Brother, everything falls apart. But not today.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/brother/text: The mephit shrieks and the cultist leaps to his feet. Then he spots the Rust Token and silences the creature with a gesture. "One of us. Next time come in the front, like a person. Sever will see you inside."
dialogues/chest:nodes/brother/text: The lid creaks and every head turns your way. A cultist reaches for his sickle, but notices the Rust Token and lowers the blade. "One of us? Then don't steal like an outsider. If you want the key, take it up with Sever."
dialogues/hask:nodes/start/choices/7/tex: [The Inscribed favor you] Kwit says I pay on time. Will you send a patrol to the east alley?
dialogues/hask:nodes/patrol_alley/text: Hask whistles for two guards with the quill seal. "The Chancery doesn't like it when its debtors come to harm. The alley will be clear before you reach the warehouse."
dialogues/hask:nodes/patrol_alley/effect: Hask sent an Inscribed patrol to the east alley. The way to the warehouse back door is clear.
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/start/choices/: I have a message for Sever from someone above. [An Inscribed patrol is tailing you]
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/let_in_token/t: The Doorkeeper turns the token over in his fingers and smiles for the first time. "The brothers from the alley… Good. I don't stop our own. Sever is inside."
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/let_in_token/e: The Doorkeeper took me for one of their own when I showed the Rust Token. The Unravelers favor me.
dialogues/sever:nodes/start/choices/6/te: [Lis] Let Lis speak. "The Echo recorded this key as a possibility that hasn't happened yet. You'd destroy something that is falling apart anyway."
factions:inscribed/desc: They register every crossing and every debt. Kwit runs the Chancery; Hask guards the gate with a patrol.
factions:inscribed/effects/friendly: Kwit sells cheaper. Hask can send a patrol to clear the east alley.
factions:inscribed/effects/wary: Kwit adds a risk surcharge. A patrol tails you, so the Doorkeeper is harder to deceive.
factions:echo/desc: The Archive of the Echo collects stories about crossings. Lis writes down every one she hears.
factions:echo/effects/friendly: Lis helps you read the records about the key (advantage on the Arcana check).
factions:echo/effects/neutral: Lis shares what she knows, but you read the records yourself.
factions:echo/effects/wary: The Archive is closed to you.
factions:unravelers/desc: A cult of decay from the old warehouse. The Doorkeeper guards the door; Sever wants the key destroyed.
factions:unravelers/effects/friendly: With a Rust Token they take you for one of their own: caught in the warehouse, you don't have to fight.
factions:unravelers/effects/neutral: They let in whoever convinces them.
factions:unravelers/effects/wary: The Doorkeeper remembers your face. Talking won't get you in any more.
maps/rusty_market:whispers/0/text: From the mist to the east comes a shuffling and a whisper: "Three lines… Is it you again?"
maps/rusty_market:whispers/1/text: A monotonous whisper carries through the warehouse walls: "Unravel, unravel, until no name remains."
maps/rusty_market:whispers/2/text: Warm air blows from under the Arch. Someone whispers a name that was once yours, but the wind scatters it before you recognize it.
maps/rusty_market:memories/0/text: Under the Arch the cobbles are worn into three parallel grooves, as if someone stood in the same spot for years.
maps/rusty_market:memories/0/journal: The cobbles under the Arch have three worn grooves. Someone stood guard here for a very long time.
maps/rusty_market:memories/1/text: The water reflects a gate that isn't behind you. When you blink, the reflection is gone.
maps/rusty_market:memories/1/journal: In the market pool I saw the reflection of a gate that isn't there.
maps/rusty_market:memories/2/text: Three faded cuts mark the alley wall, the same as the sign on your palm.
maps/rusty_market:memories/2/journal: Someone carved the sign I carry on my palm into the east alley wall.
maps/rusty_market:memories/3/text: In the dust on the warehouse floor someone has drawn three lines, over and over, as if learning them by heart.
maps/rusty_market:memories/3/journal: The Unravelers draw my sign in the dust. One of them knows who I was.
dialogues/arch:nodes/runes_fail/effects/: The runes on the Doorless Arch blurred before my eyes. Mirela or Lis at the Archive of the Echo may know what they mean.
barks:lis/10/text: This wall remembers you better than the Archive does. The key can feel it.
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/start/text: The Key Without a Door tugs in your hand toward the smooth wall between the Keyworks and the warehouses. Like frost, the outline of a door appears on the stone, a door that wasn't there a moment ago.
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/start/choice: Press the key to the outline.
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/opened/text: The key turns in the air and the door becomes real. Behind it is a cramped guardroom: a cold hearth, a bench and a ledger of crossings open at the last page. The last entry is in your handwriting: "I refused passage to the Curator. The gate is not for those who want to close it behind them." Beneath it someone has added in fresher ink: "I remember. — C."
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/opened/effec: The key opened a door in the market wall. In the old guardroom lay a ledger of crossings: the Wanderer once refused passage to the Curator, and she remembers it.
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/inside_again: The door stands in the wall as if it had always been there. The guardroom is silent and smells of cold ash.
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/faded/text: Only a pale crack in the shape of a door marks the wall. Without the key it is just stone.
items:crossings_ledger/desc: A ledger from the Wanderer's old guardroom. The last entry, in your handwriting: passage refused to the Curator.
dialogues/hask:nodes/insight_fail/effect: Hask knows something, but the Inscribed don't like questions. Others at the market talk more easily: Kwit the notary, or little Flea.
dialogues/lis:nodes/arcana_fail/effects/: The records about the key slipped away from my eyes. Maybe Mirela will tell me what the key really opens, or the runes on the Doorless Arch.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/truth_fail/effect: Mirela won't say what the Key Without a Door opens. The runes on the Doorless Arch or Lis's records in the Archive of the Echo might give it away.
maps/rusty_market:loot/0/text: At the bottom of the barrel, under a layer of rusty water, someone has tied a coin purse.
maps/rusty_market:loot/1/text: Among the rags lies a corked vial of red liquid.
maps/rusty_market:loot/2/text: An Inscribed courier's bag, slit open with a knife. Someone searched it before you, but missed a few coins in the lining.
maps/rusty_market:loot/3/text: Under the lid lie forgotten coins, probably someone's bribe that never reached its addressee.
dialogues/hask:nodes/fog/text: "Mist from the Rift. Zawias hangs over the void between the planes, and the void creeps in wherever nobody is looking. The city holds together only because someone remembers it. My gate, my market, my alley. What you see and remember stays standing. The rest is vapour and guesswork, so newcomers mostly see mist." Hask narrows his eyes. "Only there's oddly much of it around you. As if the city doesn't remember you."
dialogues/hask:nodes/fog/effects/0/journ: Hask says the violet mist is the void of the Rift between the planes. It thins where someone looks and remembers. There is suspiciously much of it around me, as if the city doesn't remember me.
dialogues/hask:nodes/start/choices/8/tex: Why is everything beyond the market drowning in this violet mist?
dialogues/arch:nodes/start/choices/0/che: The runes on the Arch blurred, but one word stayed in my head: "believe".
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/start/choices/0: The lock didn't give, but through the gap I overheard the guards: the watch at the chest changes when the bell rings. It will be easier to slip past.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/info/choices/1/chec: Kwit agrees to the trade, but still adds a "handling fee".
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/start/choices/: Opening the door, the Doorkeeper mutters that Sever hasn't slept for a week because of that key. You walk in with a surer step.
The Doorkeeper lets you in, but studies your face long and carefully.
motivations:strength/options/loyalty/des: You don't abandon your word or your people, even when it costs you.
motivations:strength/options/curiosity/d: Every door is a question, and you can't leave a question unanswered.
motivations:strength/options/compassion/: You see someone else's misery and don't walk past.
motivations:strength/options/cunning/des: The shortest way rarely goes through the front door.
motivations:flaw/options/pride/desc: You know better, and it's hard not to say so.
motivations:flaw/options/greed/desc: Every favour has a price, and yours is always higher.
motivations:flaw/options/anger/desc: Your patience runs out faster than other people's.
motivations:flaw/options/distrust/desc: Behind every smile you look for a knife.
motivations:desire/options/truth/desc: You want to know who you were before the gate spat you out.
motivations:desire/options/wealth/desc: Gold opens more doors than keys do.
motivations:desire/options/freedom/desc: No cage, no oath, no master.
motivations:desire/options/home/desc: You're looking for a place to come back to.
motivations:fear/options/oblivion/desc: You're afraid you'll vanish and nobody will notice.
motivations:fear/options/helplessness/de: The worst thing is to stand and watch, unable to do anything.
motivations:fear/options/loneliness/desc: The silence of an empty room scares you more than a fight.
motivations:fear/options/closed_doors/de: To you, a closed door means something waits on the other side.
dialogues/hask:nodes/start/choices/9/tex: What happens to those the city forgets?
dialogues/hask:nodes/oblivion/text: Hask falls silent for a moment. "They dissolve. First the name, then the face, last the shadow. I once saw someone stop being. He stood by the gate and asked if anyone knew him." He glances at your hand. "That's why I make sure people get written down here."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/reward/choices/2/: A hundred is charity. Two hundred, or find another fool.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/reward/choices/3/: I don't want gold. I want to know if there's a place for me in Zawias.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/home/text: Mirela looks at you longer than is polite. "A home? In Zawias? Everyone here is passing through." After a moment she adds, more quietly: "Bring the key back, and my door will be open to you. That's more than people usually promise here."
dialogues/odzwierny:nodes/start/choices/: I grab him by the collar and pin him to the door.
dialogues/pchla:nodes/start/choices/5/te: I give him a few coins, even if he knows nothing.
dialogues/sever:nodes/start/choices/7/te: Before we start: what do you think this key would open, if you let it?
dialogues/sever:nodes/curious/text: Sever stops sifting the dust. "You're curious. Good. I fear this key will open a place where nothing ends. Eternity without decay. Do you understand now why it has to disappear?"
dialogues/sever:nodes/curious/effects/0/: Sever fears the key will open a place where nothing ends. Maybe the argument that an unfulfilled possibility is decay too will convince him.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/start/choices/3/tex: I need a bed. (4 gp, long rest, Dorn charges you double)
dialogues/dorn:nodes/start/choices/4/tex: Dorn, the warden from your grandmother's story... It was me.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/grudge/text: Dorn reaches for a tankard and suddenly goes still. He is looking at your hand, at the three pale lines. He sets the tankard down as carefully as if it were glass. "My grandmother was supposed to cross the gate to her husband. A warden with that mark on his hand told her: 'Not today.' The next day the warden was gone, and the road to her husband's world had grown over with mist. She waited here sixty years. This inn is what that waiting built."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/grudge/choices/1/te: I don't remember it. But if it was me, I'm sorry.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/grudge/choices/2/te: Sixty years ago I wasn't even here.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/grudge/choices/3/te: Let it go, Dorn. I only came for a bed.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/grudge/choices/4/te: The warden couldn't let everyone through. Someone had to say 'no'.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/grudge/choices/5/te: Lovely story. How much did they pay you to tell it to me, of all people?
dialogues/dorn:nodes/grudge/choices/6/te: What else did she say about that warden? What was he like?
dialogues/dorn:nodes/grudge/choices/7/te: What was her husband's name? If I cross the Arch, I'll look for a trace of him.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/grudge/choices/8/te: Was she alone here, all those years?
dialogues/dorn:nodes/mark/text: Dorn grabs your wrist and turns your palm to the light. Three pale lines run across the skin, lines you never noticed before. "Grandmother drew them on every bill, in the margin, as if she was afraid she'd forget. They say the same ones are on the gate. Ask Lis at the Echo Archive, she writes such things down."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/mark/effects/1/jour: Dorn recognised the three lines on my hand. The gate warden who once turned his grandmother away had that mark. They say it is on the gate too. Lis at the Echo Archive may know more.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/sorry/text: Dorn is silent for a long time. "An apology won't do grandmother any good now." He goes back to wiping the tankard. "But nobody ever apologised to her. So... it's good someone finally said it."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/denial/text: "Maybe not." Dorn sizes you up. "Grandmother said that warden looked at people the same way. As if he wasn't really here."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/proud/text: "Someone had to." Dorn slams the tankard down. "Grandmother said he thought so too. Until one day he stopped, and simply vanished. A bed here costs two gold. For you, four."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/proud/effects/1/log: Dorn now charges you double for a bed.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/proof/text: Without a word, Dorn pulls a yellowed bill from the inn's first day out from under the counter. In the margin are three lines, drawn by a shaking hand. "Nobody pays me to remember. You pay double for a bed now."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/proof/effects/1/jou: Dorn showed me a bill from the inn's first day. His grandmother drew three lines on it, the same as the ones on my hand.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/proof/effects/2/log: Dorn now charges you double for a bed.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/truth/text: "That he wasn't cruel, just tired. Every day a queue at the gate, everyone weeping in their own way, and he alone decided. Grandmother once saw him cry when he thought nobody was looking." Dorn shrugs. "Maybe that's why he vanished."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/truth/effects/0/jou: Dorn's grandmother remembered the warden with three lines as tired, not cruel. Every day he alone decided who would cross the gate, until he vanished.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/promise/text: Dorn looks at you as if weighing a coin. "Ardan. A shipwright from Tin Bay." After a moment he adds: "Don't promise if you won't keep it. In Zawias, promises aren't forgotten."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/promise/effects/1/j: I promised Dorn that beyond the Arch I would look for a trace of Ardan, a shipwright from Tin Bay, his grandmother's husband.
dialogues/dorn:nodes/lonely/text: "Alone? In an inn?" For the first time, Dorn smiles. "Never. She said a tavern is a home for those who got stuck. Full of strangers, but nobody has to eat alone." He sets a tankard in front of you. "This one's on the house."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/confess/text: Dorn wipes the same tankard for a long time. "Grandmother said that if she ever met him again, she wouldn't know whether to hit him or thank him. After that day, nobody ever had to ask anyone for passage again." He sets the tankard down. "I don't know either. Sleep here as long as you like. Pay like everyone else."
dialogues/dorn:nodes/confess/effects/2/j: I told Dorn that I was the warden who turned his grandmother away. He doesn't know whether to forgive me, but he charges me for a bed like everyone else again.
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/start/choice: Before I do anything, I press my ear to the wall. I have to know what's on the other side.
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/listen/text: The stone is as cold as well water. On the other side something rustles softly, as if a draught were turning pages. Then you hear a whisper, tired and familiar: "Not today." You recognise that voice. It is your own.
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/listen/effec: Through the wall by the outline of the door I heard my own voice whispering: "Not today." Behind that door someone, or something, remembers who I was.
dialogues/hidden_door:nodes/listen/choic: Press the key to the outline.
dialogues/arch:nodes/with_key/choices/2/: No oath binds me any more. Not even that one.
dialogues/arch:nodes/freedom/text: The Arch does not answer, but the trembling beneath it quiets, as if it were listening. You remember the words of the oath: "The road belongs to those who walk it." It was not a cage, but a door you left open for others. Now you stand on this side, and nobody can tell you 'not today'.
dialogues/arch:nodes/freedom/choices/0/t: Raise the key and turn it in the air beneath the arch.
dialogues/mirela:nodes/truth/choices/3/t: And how much would the highest bidder pay for it?
dialogues/mirela:nodes/price/text: Mirela gives a short snort of laughter. "More than either of us will see in a lifetime. But a merchant won't give it back to me when the Custodian asks where it is." She sighs. "Fine. You didn't sell it, so I won't be stingy either. A hundred and fifty, and not a word to anyone."
dialogues/mirela:nodes/price/effects/1/l: Mirela raises the reward to 150 gp.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/info/choices/4/text: Write this down, Kwit: "The Inscribed knew about the theft and kept quiet." I wonder how much a sentence like that weighs in your register.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/cunning/text: The quill stops mid-letter. Kwit stares at the blot for a long time. "A sentence nobody has signed weighs nothing." He sets the quill down. "But I won't test how many signers you'd find. The Unravelers. The old warehouse in the east. Their leader is called Sever. I'm not recording this conversation."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/cunning/effects/2/j: I offered Kwit a sentence he wouldn't want to see in the register. For free, he pointed me to the Unravelers' warehouse in the east and their leader, Sever.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/cunning/choices/0/t: A pleasure doing business with you.
dialogues/pchla:nodes/start/choices/6/te: Someone's forcing you into something, aren't they? I won't just stand and watch. Tell me who.
words:mirela_key/text: I promised Mirela I would come back with the Key Without a Door.
words:pchla_silence/text: I promised Flea I wouldn't say who warned me.
words:dorn_ardan/text: I promised Dorn that beyond the Arch I would look for a trace of Ardan.
words:kwit_custodian/text: I told Kwit the Custodian sent me.
words:doorkeeper_message/text: I told the Doorkeeper I had a message for Sever from someone up above.
words:token_brothers/text: I showed the Doorkeeper the Rust Token and passed on greetings from the brothers in the alley.
dialogues/kwit:nodes/start/choices/5/tex: The Inscribed keep a register of everything. What does it say about me?
dialogues/kwit:nodes/ledger/text: Kwit turns a page of the register, then another. "Nothing. Not a single word given, not a single word broken. Either you're very careful, or nobody here has needed you yet."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/ledger_open/text: Kwit taps his quill on a column. "A word given, not yet repaid. The Inscribed like people with debts: you always know where to find them." He smiles thinly. "Reality is a contract. You are signing yours right now."
dialogues/kwit:nodes/ledger_bad/text: Kwit doesn't even need to open the register. "A broken word, or a lie that came to light. In the register that's a hole in the contract, and the wind blows straight through it." The quill scratches. "Every word you say from now on will weigh less."
dialogues/lis:nodes/start/choices/7/text: What will the Echo write about me?
dialogues/lis:nodes/companion/choices/3/: What will the Echo write about me?
dialogues/lis:nodes/words/text: Lis runs a finger down the book, and the letters line up beneath it like obedient dogs. "So far your words match what you do. That's rare in the Archive. Most stories lie in their very first sentence."
dialogues/lis:nodes/words/choices/0/text: Let's hope it stays that way.
dialogues/lis:nodes/words_lies/text: Lis looks into the book for a long time. "The Echo records what was said, not what was true. Your lies are here too, as clear as the rest, even if nobody caught them." She closes the book. "The Inscribed only know the ones that came to light. We remember them all."
barks:hask/5/text: Mirela's asking at the gate about someone who promised to come back. Is that nice?
barks:dorn/2/text: Ardan. A shipwright from Tin Bay. Remember?
barks:mirela/3/text: You promised you'd come back with the key. I'm waiting.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/text: The key burns again, and the memory returns, clearer than before. A warden stands at the gate with three fresh cuts on his palm. He has your face, only tired in a way you haven't had time to be. The queue of supplicants dissolves into the mist. The warden looks straight at you. "Tomorrow I give the gate my name. You know I did it. So tell me: why?"
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/0/t: Because no one should decide alone who crosses.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/1/t: Because you were tired. Every 'no' took something from you.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/2/t: I don't know. That's why I'm here.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/3/t: Because you promised people a road, and your name stood in its way.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/4/t: Because you wanted to see what was on the other side. Alone, not as a warden.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/5/t: Because you couldn't bear to watch them weep in the queue any more.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/6/t: Because it was the only way no one could ever force you to choose again.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/7/t: Because you knew better than the gate and wanted to prove it.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/8/t: Because for your name you got something more precious: a life without debts.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/9/t: Because you'd had enough. Of everyone. Of yourself too.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/10/: Because you trusted no one who would come after you. Better that no one had that power.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/11/: Because you wanted to know who you are without a title.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/12/: Because a warden owns nothing, and you wanted everything.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/13/: Because your name was a chain that bound you to the gate.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/14/: Because a warden has no home, and you wanted one.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/15/: Because you were afraid that only the title would remain, and nobody would remember the person.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/16/: Because every 'not today' meant standing and watching and doing nothing.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/17/: Because at the gate you always stood alone.
dialogues/memory:nodes/start/choices/18/: Because you had become a door that closed on others.
dialogues/memory:nodes/why_power/text: The warden nods slowly. "That's what I keep telling myself. That power over the road is too much for one hand. It's good to hear it wasn't just an excuse."
dialogues/memory:nodes/why_tired/text: The warden looks away. "Every day someone wept in a different way. I thought nobody saw it." After a moment he adds: "Tiredness is an honest reason. Not a pretty one, but honest."
dialogues/memory:nodes/why_unknown/text: The warden smiles for the first time, crookedly, like someone recognising his own joke. "I wasn't sure either. Maybe that's why I gave up my name and not my memory."
dialogues/memory:nodes/why_strength/text: "So I gave up my name to stay who I really was." The warden looks at his hand. "Strange. I thought it would be a loss."
dialogues/memory:nodes/why_flaw/text: The warden snorts softly. "So it wasn't nobility. Good. I wouldn't have believed in nobility."
dialogues/memory:nodes/why_desire/text: "I wanted something for myself. For the first time in years." The warden clenches his cut hand. "I hope you found it."
dialogues/memory:nodes/why_fear/text: The warden is silent for a long time. "I was afraid. Yes. A warden who is afraid shouldn't hold the gate."
dialogues/memory:nodes/word/text: "An oath is a word too. Tomorrow I give it to the gate, and I'll keep it." The warden leans towards you. "And you? Did you keep your word here?"
dialogues/memory:nodes/word/choices/1/te: No. I broke my word, or I lied.
dialogues/memory:nodes/word/choices/3/te: I gave no one my word here.
dialogues/memory:nodes/word_clean/text: The warden looks at you as if reading a register you cannot see. "True. Few come to the gate with clean hands."
dialogues/memory:nodes/word_owned/text: "At least you're not lying to me." The warden nods. "A word that broke, and that you own up to, weighs more than one nobody ever checked."
dialogues/memory:nodes/word_lied/text: The warden looks at you for a long time. "You're lying. I know, because I once lied the same way." There is no anger in it, only weariness. "Fooling yourself is the hardest thing. And the easiest."
dialogues/memory:nodes/word_none/text: "Careful." The warden almost smiles. "I was careful too, until I gave my word to the gate."
dialogues/memory:nodes/now/text: The mist creeps closer. "Tomorrow I won't have a name. You already have another." The warden tilts his head. "Who are you now?"
dialogues/memory:nodes/now/choices/0/tex: Whoever they call me today. Leave that other name to the gate.
dialogues/memory:nodes/now/choices/1/tex: The Wanderer. I want back what I gave away.
dialogues/memory:nodes/now/choices/2/tex: I don't know yet. But I'll be the one to decide.
dialogues/memory:nodes/fade/text: The warden nods, as if he heard exactly what he expected. "Then the road belongs to you." The memory fades. What remains is warmth in your palm and a key that has stopped trembling.
dialogues/memory:nodes/fade/effects/1/jo: In the memory I spoke with myself from before the oath. He asked why I gave up my name, whether I kept my word here, and who I am now.
words:self_kept/text: I told myself I had kept every word.

encounters:ambush/on_defeat/3/journal: The bandits from the alley left me in the mist and took half my gold. Before I drifted off, I heard them heading back to the Unravelers' warehouse in the east.
encounters:warehouse/on_defeat/4/journal: The Unravelers unravelled me into mist. They shut the warehouse doors, and Sever moved the key to the bottom of his chest. Stealing it will be harder.
dialogues/chest:nodes/start/choices/2/te: Open it quietly. Sever has hidden the key at the very bottom.
dialogues/backdoor:nodes/picked/choices/: Sneak to the chest. Sever has hidden the key at the very bottom.
dialogues/rift:nodes/start/text: The pain fades, and your name fades with it. The void is quiet and warm as forgetting. Somewhere very far away someone speaks a word that might have been you, but you don't catch the end of it. Then the gate draws breath.
dialogues/rift:nodes/fall/text: The pain fades and the city stops remembering you. You unravel into mist, thread by thread, and the Rusty Market drifts away like a distant shore. Something moves in the void. Someone has been waiting for you here.
dialogues/rift:nodes/queue/text: You hear the queue at the gate. A woman with a child in her arms begs to cross. Your own voice, tired and strange, answers: "Not today." The child looks at you as if learning your face by heart. Then the gate draws breath.
dialogues/rift:nodes/queue/effects/1/jou: In the mist from the Rift I saw the queue at the gate. I refused passage to a woman with a child. The child looked at me as if wanting to remember me.
dialogues/rift:nodes/fall_again/text: The pain fades and the city forgets you again. This time the void knows the way. It leads you through the mist until the mist thickens into walls of stone.
dialogues/rift:nodes/ledger/text: It is the warden's room. You are writing in the ledger of crossings, and your hand trembles. You count one day's refusals: forty-three. You close the ledger and for the first time you think of giving the gate your name. Then the gate draws breath.
dialogues/rift:nodes/ledger/effects/1/jo: In the mist I saw the warden's room and the ledger of crossings. In one day I refused forty-three times. That was when I first thought of giving up my name.
